match.reason: The new point combines evaporation, crystallisation and distillation in one card, but the closest bank points each cover only part of it: sci-evaporation-crystallisation lacks distillation, and sci-distillation-chromatography lacks evaporation and crystallisation and adds chromatography, so no single point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Evaporation, crystallisation and distillation
card: Heating a solution turns the liquid solvent into a gas, which escapes into the air. The dissolved solid is left behind in the dish.
If a solution is left to evaporate slowly, the solid forms crystals as the liquid goes. Fast heating tends to leave a powder instead.
The solution is heated until the liquid boils. The gas travels into a cooled tube, where it condenses back into a pure liquid that is collected in a separate container.
Evaporation keeps the solid and loses the liquid. Distillation keeps the liquid, and the solid stays behind in the flask.
draft.remember: Evaporation keeps the dissolved solid. Distillation collects the liquid.

a.q: Kai heats salty water in a dish until all the water has gone. What is left in the dish?
opts: The salt that was dissolved in the water
A pure liquid collected from the water
Salt and water mixed together evenly
Nothing, because the salt turns to gas too
a.why: The water turns to gas and escapes, but the dissolved salt stays in the dish. The mixture is not left unchanged, because the water has gone.
a.clue: What escapes into the air when the solution is heated?

b.q: Mia has seawater and wants to collect drinkable water from it. Which method should she use, and why?
opts: Distillation, because the boiled water is cooled and kept
Evaporation, because the water is left behind in the dish
Distillation, because the salt boils off and is collected
Evaporation, because the water is cooled into a pure liquid
b.why: Distillation boils the water off and cools it back into a liquid, which is collected. Evaporation lets the water escape into the air, so it is lost and only the salt is left.
b.clue: Which method collects the liquid rather than losing it?

wants.brief: A distillation set-up. A flask of salty solution sits on a heat source. A tube leads from the flask into a cooled tube, labelled condenser, and then into a collecting container labelled pure liquid. The flask is labelled solution, with the dissolved solid staying behind. Arrows show the gas moving along the tube.
wants.why: It shows how the liquid boils off, cools and is collected separately from the solid.

a.best: The salt that was dissolved in the water

b.best: Distillation, because the boiled water is cooled and kept
